approve_invoice.description: Approve a draft invoice, which makes it final and records it in the books. An invoice has to be approved before a payment can be recorded against it. This cannot be undone.

parameters.description: The invoice's Wave ID. 'List invoices' returns these in 'invoice_ids', and 'Create invoice' reports the one it made as 'invoice_id'.

archive_product.description: Archive a product or service so it stops being offered on new invoices. Wave has no product delete: a product that has ever been invoiced is part of the books, so archiving is the only removal there is.
archive_product.name: archive_product

parameters.description: The product or service's Wave ID. 'List products' returns these in 'product_ids'.

create_customer.description: Add a customer to a business. Only the name is required; everything else - contact details, billing address, currency - can be filled in later with 'Update customer'.

create_invoice.description: Create an invoice for a customer. A draft can still be edited in Wave and is not in the books yet; approving it makes it final. Every line item needs a product - use 'List products' or 'Create product' to get one.

parameters.description: Which set of books to work in. Pick from the list; the value sent is the business's Wave ID. 'List businesses' returns these in 'business_ids'.
parameters.name: business_id

parameters.description: The customer's Wave ID. 'List customers' returns these in 'customer_ids', and every create/update step reports the one it touched as 'customer_id'.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: The lines on the invoice, as a list of objects. Each needs "product_id"; "quantity", "unit_price", "description" and "sales_tax_ids" are optional and fall back to the product's own. For example: [{"product_id": "UHJvZHVjdDo0MzIx", "quantity": 2}].
parameters.name: items

parameters.description: Whether the invoice starts as an editable draft or is approved straight away. Approval cannot be undone - an approved invoice is deleted rather than returned to draft.
parameters.name: status

options.label: Draft - editable, and not yet in the books
Approved - final, and recorded in the books

parameters.description: When the invoice is issued. Defaults to today.

parameters.description: Leave empty to let Wave take the next number after the highest one it has.
parameters.name: invoice_number

parameters.description: The customer's purchase or sales order number.
parameters.name: po_number

parameters.description: The heading at the top of the document. Leave empty for the business's default.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: The line under the title. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: subhead

parameters.description: Notes shown to the customer on the invoice.
parameters.name: memo

parameters.description: Text along the bottom of the invoice.
parameters.name: footer

parameters.description: The currency to use. Leave empty to use the business's own currency, which is what almost every workflow wants.
parameters.name: currency

status.description: The status it was created in

create_product.description: Add a product or service to a business. Attach an income account to make it sellable - Wave will not put a product with no income account on an invoice.
create_product.name: create_product

parameters.description: Which set of books to work in. Pick from the list; the value sent is the business's Wave ID. 'List businesses' returns these in 'business_ids'.
parameters.name: business_id

parameters.description: What the product or service is called.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Price for one unit, in the ordinary currency amount - 12.50, not 1250.
parameters.name: unit_price

parameters.description: What appears under the name on an invoice line. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: Which income account the sales of this product post to. Attaching one is what makes a product sellable - Wave will not put a product with no income account on an invoice. Wave accepts only accounts whose subtype is INCOME, DISCOUNTS, OTHER_INCOME; each option's subtype is shown in square brackets.
parameters.name: income_account_id

parameters.description: Which expense account purchases of this product post to, which is what lets it go on a bill. Wave accepts only accounts whose subtype is EXPENSE, COST_OF_GOODS_SOLD, PAYMENT_PROCESSING_FEES, PAYROLL_EXPENSES; each option's subtype is shown in square brackets.
parameters.name: expense_account_id

parameters.description: Sales taxes applied to this product by default whenever it goes on an invoice. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: sales_tax_ids

delete_customer.description: Delete a customer. Wave refuses while any invoice or payment still points at them, so delete those first - a customer who has traded is part of the books.
delete_customer.name: delete_customer

delete_invoice.description: Delete an invoice. Wave refuses while payments are still recorded against it, so remove those first - 'Get invoice' lists them in 'payment_ids'.

parameters.name: invoice_id

delete_invoice_payment.description: Remove a recorded payment from an invoice, putting the amount back on what is owed. 'Get invoice' lists an invoice's payment IDs in 'payment_ids'.
delete_invoice_payment.name: delete_invoice_payment

parameters.description: The payment's Wave ID. 'Get invoice' returns these in 'payment_ids', and 'Record invoice payment' reports the one it made as 'payment_id'.
parameters.name: payment_id
